source: Ported from agent-lab .devcontainer/bootstrap-linux.sh (node, uv, gh, codex, claude) plus fresh 2026-09-22 fetches for qmd, mcporter, rtk, ai-memory, context-mode. Each archive was downloaded into a disposable worktree temp directory and hashed with sha256sum; npm entries were additionally cross-checked against `npm view <pkg> dist.integrity` (sha512, base64) computed with `openssl dgst -sha512 -binary | base64` over the same downloaded tarball -- all five matched exactly.
schema_v2_note: 2026-09-25 (W1 track switch, docs/tasks/sota-rollout-20260925): migrated in place from schema_version 1. Every id/version/kind/url/sha256/install_note value below is byte-for-byte unchanged from the v1 record reviewed_at 2026-09-22 except for the corrections dated 2026-09-25 in this fix round's own install_note amendments (root_name/entrypoints[].in_root, checked read-only against the live ECO_INSTALL_ROOT: see each amended entry's own note); only new fields (root_name, current_link, entrypoints, surfaces, state_dirs, window, rollback_class) and the new top-level candidates/supersedes/divergence sections were added otherwise. adoption/pins-schema-v2.json documents every new field; adoption/tools/ecosystem-switch reads root_name/current_link/entrypoints/surfaces/state_dirs/window/rollback_class as its component spec (adopt --baseline/--relink). A field whose value could not be verified from this checkout's own primary sources (the bootstrap script that installs it, and this pin's own install_note) carries a nested {"status": "pending"} marker instead of a fabricated value, per switch.md: 'unknown fields for other winners can be filled later by the qualify wave (mark pending)'. scripts/validate.py's pins-v2 parity check itself never inspects entrypoints[]/state_dirs[]/surfaces[] at all (nested or otherwise) -- it only compares each tools[].id/version against manifests/stack.json and catalogs/landscape/*.json winners[].pin, and separately requires every top-level candidates[] entry's own status to be exactly "pending" (report-only there too); a nested pending marker inside a tools[] entry's own sub-fields is informational for ecosystem-switch's own readers (e.g. adopt --relink already skips an entrypoint whose in_root is null) and is not itself re-validated by that parity check.

minimum version; native auto-update on the latest channel. Verified by downloading the linux-x64 binary directly and independently computing its sha256 (2026-09-23), matching both this pin and the 2.1.280 manifest.json's linux-x64 checksum. Superseded the prior npm-wrapper pin (2.1.278, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1) once the native installer became the reference path: fetch the binary, verify its sha256, then run `"$bin" install 2.1.280`, matching ~/codex-ecosystem/bin/bootstrap-linux.sh's own claude-code step. The installed binary self-manages ~/.local/share/claude/versions and the ~/.local/bin/claude launcher and auto-updates on the latest channel from there; this pin is a floor, not a ceiling, and no DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER opt-out is set.

entrypoints.note: divergence native-auto-update: the live entrypoint is ~/.local/bin/claude, a launcher the native installer itself manages under ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version> (outside ECO_INSTALL_ROOT); adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh install_native() writes a redirecting bin/claude script only when bin_dir differs from ~/.local/bin. ecosystem-switch does not manage a current/claude-code link (see divergence[] below).

tools.install_note: 2026-09-23 catalog-winner-but-unpinned gap: this host already has markitdown 0.1.7 (Microsoft's Office/PDF/HTML-to-Markdown converter), installed as a uv tool: its uv-receipt.toml requires markitdown==0.1.7 with no-build, and its console script's shebang points into the tool's own virtualenv. The artifact at the URL above was re-downloaded and sha256-hashed independently; it matches PyPI's published digest (https://pypi.org/pypi/markitdown/0.1.7/json urls[].digests.sha256, read 2026-09-23). install_pin's *-uv-tool case runs `uv tool install --python 3.13 markitdown==0.1.7` into UV_TOOL_DIR, so the entry point runs in its own environment. uv resolves the pinned version from PyPI and does not check this sha256; it is recorded as an independent artifact cross-check and satisfies this catalog's fail-closed null-sha256 refusal.

entrypoints.note: uv-managed tool environment (UV_TOOL_DIR/python-tools, UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR=bin_dir); uv itself owns the entry-point shim and the versioned virtualenv it points at, so there is no discrete tools/<id>-<version> root for ecosystem-switch's current/<id> indirection to wrap. A future qualify wave that wants switch-managed cutover for a uv-tool pin needs either two side-by-side UV_TOOL_DIR prefixes or an ecosystem-switch operation kind this track did not add.
